How much effort it costs to engage in activity

tags.description: Involves playing something on some website

activities.description: Play games on websites such as https://sketchful.io/. One person draws something and another person guesses what is being drawn.
First choose categories, then one person invents something from that category, another person has to guess what that is by asking questions. Questions can be answered only as yes or no.
Take turns asking 'Would you rather...' questions with 2 clearly different options. The other person has to choose and say why they made that choice. Switch roles.
First, choose a fictional world, theme, or a prompt. Then, pretend to be fictional characters in that setting.

Find personality tests on online websites such as https://www.idrlabs.com/tests.php. Choose a test with a silly theme (for example, character test or villain test). Solve the test. Before sending results, try to guess what results would other person get. Check if you were right.

Find personality tests on online websites such as https://www.idrlabs.com/tests.php. Choose a test which is more serious (for example, enneagram or big 5 inventory). Solve the test. Before sending results, try to guess what results would other person get. Check if you were right.

Draw another person and self using image generation https://perchance.org/ai-text-to-image-generator. Send used prompt, and generated image of both for comments. See whether you had a realistic mental image of other person.
One person asks question, another responds. Later persons switch.
One person asks question, another responds. Later persons switch. The questions have to follow a light theme. Example: 'Which is your favourite season?'
One person asks question, another responds. Later persons switch. The questions have to be about deep topics. Example: 'Which philosophical school is closest to your views?'
One person asks question, another responds. Later persons switch. The questions have to be weird and odd. Example: 'When borrowing someones shadow, is it necessary to give it back later?'
One person asks question, another responds. Later persons switch. The questions have to be embarrassing.

One person asks question, another responds. Later persons switch. The response has to be lyrics copied from a song. Example: 'What is a thought which was following you for some time?' 'Now it's time to eat soft ice cream'
One person asks question, another responds. Later persons switch. The response has to be only emojis. Example: 'What is your mood right now?' '😴🌓🥱🌛🛌💤🍵'

How could the future be like 10 years from now? What could be different? What could be same? Ask a question, other person has to make a prediction. Switch. Example: 'Would people still have to work?' 'Yes, but some wealthy countries might have UBI'
One person chooses a question from https://en.wikiversity.org/wiki/Knowing_Someone/Big_Talk, you both have to respond to it. Later who chooses switches.
One person gives a challenge which should be quick to do. Another shows proof of completion. Later persons switch. Example challange: find nearest blue item and send its image.
Choose a prompt of a story from a LLM. Then, one person writes 2-3 sentences of that story. Another person has to continue in similar way. Later persons switch.
Write 3 things which happened recently. 1 of these can be weird or false, and others are normal or genuine. Other person has to guess which was odd one. Later switch.
Give 3 statements about yourself. Two are true and one is a lie. Other person guesses which is a lie, then asks a follow-up question that could expose the lie. Switch.
What is a controversial or edgy opinion which you have?
Next few messages which you send, have to be only images
Next few messages which you send, have to be only lines from lyrics of any songs
Choose a style. Next few messages have to adhere to that theme. Examples: old-fashined, silly, random

Choose a topic. Exchange what is interesting about your country or region in relation to that. Examples of topics: habits, specifics, language, monuments, history, nature, landmarks, famous people, cuisine
Call with voice through Discord

One person suggests what kind of media to choose - which genre and what kind of media. Another person chooses a specific title. Read it and discuss it later. Example genres: thriller, mystery, historical, comedy. Example content: book, blog post, article, manga, song.
If you subscribe to interesting profiles on some platform, share them to other person. It can be a platform such as Substack, or other.

Choose a theme. Then you have to exchange compliments, but themed around that topic. It is OK if they are cringe. Example: theme of stars and astronomy, 'your positivity and brigthness glisten like a supernova'
One person takes short time to explain a weird or interesting topic as if giving a TED Talk, then the other asks a 'clarifying question'. Switch. Example topic: internet culture of 2020s
Choose a starting and ending entity. Example: cactus, bomb. Then you have to connect them using 6 or less steps 'is related to'.
One person chooses a topic. Example: 'should schools have uniforms'. The other gives 3 fast pros and 3 fast cons. They have to be written as first thought. Then try again and swap roles.

Each person has to admit something embarrassing. Examples: a guilty pleasure, unpopular opinion, awkward moment, silly habit. The other responds by admitting to something that is connected to that in some way. Keep it light and judgment-free.
Ask LLM for elements of a story. It would be better if they were somehow random. Example: tropical island, vines, horror. Then, write quickly a short story for few sentences using these elements.

One person says a word, the other responds with the first word that comes to mind. Continue back-and-forth for 10-20 exchanges. Then analyze the chain to see what patterns or unexpected connections emerged.

One person presents increasingly difficult 'choose one or lose it forever' scenarios. Example: books, foods, abilities, memories. The other must decide and briefly explain why. Take turns being the questioner.
One person gives a description of something, but purposefully awful. Other person tries to guess what it is. Switch.
Take turns posing scenarios. Each person has to say whether they would survive them, and why.
Open an AI image generator. One person generates background image, another generates a caption.
Share a recent dream, and decode it with help of another person.
Describe something cringe and shameful that you do. Another person comments whether it is really bad or not. Switch.
Pose a hypothetical, and each person elaborates on the consequences. Examples: 'What if cats could talk?' 'What if anime was real?' 'What if you could rewind time?'
If you could make 3 things become true, which things would you choose?
Describe a real or imaginary place where you feel calm and safe. Paint a picture with words, the sounds, smells, textures. Let the other person ask questions to explore it before falling asleep.
Each person names 3 things they appreciate right now, then briefly explains why.
Take turns naming favorite sleepy things, like pajamas, blankets, nighttime sounds, or pre-sleep rituals.
Find one small comforting object nearby and show or describe it. The other person does the same.
Close your eyes for a moment and describe a peaceful place you would like to be resting in.
Say the first chaotic thought that enters your head, then the other person responds with an equally odd one.
Take turns describing one harmless thing you did that somehow caused chaos, confusion, or social damage.
